examples.en: The child opened the door and stepped right in.
The teacher strode toward me.

examples.ko: 벌써 봄이 성큼 다가온 것 같아요.
examples.en: It feels like spring has suddenly arrived.

examples.ko: 그는 망설이지 않고 앞으로 성큼 나섰어요.
examples.en: Without hesitating, he stepped forward boldly.
The young people strode along even while carrying loads.
The exam is almost here, so I'm in a hurry.

explain: 다리를 크게 벌려 걷는 모습뿐 아니라 계절이나 시험처럼 때가 갑자기 가까워질 때도 '성큼 다가오다'라고 많이 말해요. 걸음이 계속 이어질 때는 '성큼성큼'을 써요.
explain_en: It describes a big stride, but it is also very common for time that suddenly gets close, as in '성큼 다가오다' for a season or an exam. When the strides keep going, use '성큼성큼'.

examples.en: During puberty, a lot of sex hormones are produced.
As you get older, sex hormone secretion decreases.

examples.ko: 성호르몬은 몸의 변화에 큰 영향을 줘요.
examples.en: Sex hormones have a big effect on changes in the body.
I had a sex hormone test at the hospital.
They say my sex hormone level is lower than normal.

examples.ko: 운동을 하면 성호르몬 균형에 도움이 된다고 해요.
examples.en: They say exercise helps balance sex hormones.

explain: 주로 건강, 의학, 과학 수업에서 나오는 말이라 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '호르몬'이라고 할 때가 많아요. '성호르몬이 나오다/분비되다', '성호르몬 수치'처럼 써요.
explain_en: This word mostly appears in health, medicine and science classes, so in everyday talk people often just say '호르몬'. Common patterns are '성호르몬이 나오다/분비되다' and '성호르몬 수치'.

examples.ko: 회사가 제품을 세계화하면서 해외 지점도 늘렸어요.
examples.en: As the company took its products global, it also added overseas branches.

examples.ko: 음식을 세계화하다가 고유의 맛이 사라진다고 걱정하는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people worry that a food's original taste is lost while it is being taken global.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 한국 음식을 세계화하고 싶어 해요.
examples.en: This restaurant wants to take Korean food global.

examples.ko: 그 회사가 한국 드라마를 세계화한 덕분에 팬이 늘었어요.
examples.en: Thanks to that company taking Korean dramas global, the fans increased.

examples.ko: 우리 전통 음식을 어떻게 세계화할 수 있을까요?
examples.en: How can we make our traditional food go global?
To go global, you first need to study foreign languages.

explain: '세계화'는 세상이 하나로 이어지는 흐름을 말할 때도 쓰고, '세계화하다'는 어떤 것을 세계로 널리 퍼뜨릴 때 자주 써요. 비슷한 '국제화'는 나라들 사이의 교류나 기준에 초점이 있고, '글로벌화'는 같은 뜻으로 더 가볍게 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: '세계화' is used for the trend of the world becoming connected, and '세계화하다' often means to spread something widely across the world. '국제화' focuses more on exchange and standards between countries, while '글로벌화' is a lighter, more casual way to say the same thing.

examples.ko: 작은 방을 세내서 혼자 살고 있어요.
examples.en: I rent a small room and live alone.
My friend and I decided to rent a house together.
To rent a shop, you need a deposit.
I rented a studio apartment near school.

examples.ko: 세내는 사람이 많아서 방이 금방 나가요.
examples.en: Many people want to rent, so rooms go quickly.
It's a rented house, so I can't fix it as I like.

explain: 돈을 내고 집이나 방을 빌려 쓰는 쪽이 '세내다'이고, 빌려주는 쪽은 '세주다'나 '세놓다'예요. 요즘 말로는 '월세로 얻다', '방을 구하다'처럼 말하는 경우가 더 많아요.
explain_en: '세내다' is for the person who pays to use a house or room, while the person who lends it out says '세주다' or '세놓다'. In everyday speech people often say '월세로 얻다' or '방을 구하다' instead.

examples.en: You have to apply for the documents under the householder's name.
The householder of our home is my father.
If the householder changes, you have to report it to the community center.
It's a subsidy that only the householder can apply for.
After I got married, I became the householder.

examples.ko: 서류에 세대주와의 관계를 쓰는 칸이 있어요.
examples.en: The form has a box for your relationship to the householder.

explain: 주민등록이나 각종 신청서처럼 공식적인 서류에서 많이 나오는 말이에요. 집에서 평소에 '가장'이라고 부르는 사람과 같을 때가 많지만, 세대주는 서류상의 이름이라 꼭 가장 돈을 많이 버는 사람이라는 뜻은 아니에요.
explain_en: This word mostly appears in official paperwork such as resident registration and applications. It is often the same person people call the head of the family at home, but it is a paperwork term and does not necessarily mean the top earner.

examples.en: It's convenient to leave tax filing to a tax accountant.
I booked a consultation at the tax accountant's office.
I found a tax accountant when I started my own business.
The tax accountant checked the documents carefully for me.

examples.ko: 우리 가게는 세무사와 계약해서 장부를 관리해요.
examples.en: Our shop has a contract with a tax accountant who manages our books.
I asked how much a tax accountant would cost.

explain: 세금 신고와 납부를 도와주는 전문가를 말해요. 가게나 회사를 하는 사람은 '세무사 사무실'에 일을 맡기는 경우가 많아요. 돈의 흐름을 정리하고 검토하는 일을 하는 '회계사'와는 하는 일이 조금 달라요.
explain_en: This is the professional who helps with tax filing and payment. People who run shops or companies often leave the work to a '세무사 사무실'. It is a bit different from a '회계사' (accountant), who focuses on organizing and reviewing financial records.

examples.en: I filled a washbowl with water and washed my face.

examples.ko: 할머니 댁에는 아직도 낡은 세숫대야가 있어요.
examples.en: Grandma's house still has an old washbowl.
Please wipe the used washbowl clean and leave it.

examples.ko: 아기 목욕을 시킬 때 큰 세숫대야를 써요.
examples.en: I use a large washbowl when bathing the baby.
I put the soup in a bowl as big as a washbowl.
I left the laundry soaking in the washbowl.

explain: 세수할 때 물을 담는 넓은 그릇이에요. 말할 때는 그냥 '대야'라고 하는 사람도 많고, 발을 씻거나 빨래를 담글 때도 같은 그릇을 써요. 큰 그릇을 놀리듯 말할 때 '세숫대야만 하다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is a wide basin for water used when washing your face. In speech many people just say '대야', and the same basin is used for washing feet or soaking laundry. You can also say '세숫대야만 하다' to jokingly describe something very large.

examples.en: The cube of 2 is 8.
If you cube 3, it becomes 27.
The unit of volume is the cubic centimeter.
We practiced cube calculations in math class.
The volume of a cube with sides of 4 is 4 cubed.
Do you know what the cubed value of the number is?

explain: '제곱'은 같은 수를 두 개 곱하는 것(3×3)이고, 세제곱은 같은 수를 세 개 곱하는 것(3×3×3)이에요. '세제곱미터', '세제곱센티미터'처럼 부피 단위에도 써요. '~를 세제곱하다'로 동사처럼도 써요.
explain_en: '제곱' means multiplying two copies of a number (3×3), while '세제곱' means multiplying three copies (3×3×3). It is also used in volume units like '세제곱미터' and '세제곱센티미터'. You can use it like a verb as in '~를 세제곱하다'.

examples.ko: 안 쓰는 방을 세줘서 용돈을 벌어요.
examples.en: I rent out the unused room to earn some pocket money.
I listed my house with a realtor to rent it out.
I rented out the first floor of the building to a shop.

examples.ko: 방 한 칸을 학생에게 세주고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm renting out one room to a student.

examples.ko: 이사 가는 동안 집을 세줄까 생각 중이에요.
examples.en: I'm thinking of renting out the house while I'm away.
Rent comes in every month from the house I rented out.

explain: 집이나 방을 빌려주는 쪽이 쓰는 말이고, 빌리는 쪽은 '세내다'를 써요. '세놓다'도 거의 같은 뜻으로 많이 말해요. 조금 딱딱한 말로는 '임대하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: This is used by the person lending a house or room, while the person borrowing it says '세내다'. '세놓다' is another common word with almost the same meaning. A more formal word is '임대하다'.

examples.en: My monthly pay after tax is 3 million won.
How much do you get as an annual salary after tax?

examples.ko: 광고에 나온 금액이 세후인지 꼭 확인하세요.
examples.en: Be sure to check whether the amount in the ad is after tax.
The after-tax profit was less than I expected.
This number is after tax, not before tax.

examples.ko: 세후로 계산하면 한 달에 250만 원쯤 남아요.
examples.en: Calculated after tax, about 2.5 million won is left each month.

explain: 월급이나 연봉 이야기에서 가장 많이 나와요. 반대말은 '세전'이고, 취업 정보에서는 둘을 꼭 구분해서 봐야 해요. 실제로 손에 들어오는 돈은 '세후' 금액이에요.
explain_en: It appears most often when talking about monthly or annual pay. The opposite is '세전' (before tax), and in job listings you should always check which one is meant. The money you actually receive is the '세후' amount.

examples.en: I added a little celery to the salad.

examples.ko: 셀러리는 향이 강해서 안 먹는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Celery has a strong smell, so some people don't eat it.
Please slice the celery stalks thinly.
I bought a bunch of celery at the supermarket.
I drink celery juice every morning.
Celery and onions go into this soup.

explain: 표준 표기는 '셀러리'예요. '샐러리'라고 쓰면 월급을 뜻하는 영어 salary가 떠올라 헷갈릴 수 있으니 조심하세요. 한국 음식에는 자주 안 쓰지만 샐러드나 주스에 많이 넣어요.
explain_en: The standard spelling is '셀러리'. Writing '샐러리' can be confused with the English word salary, so be careful. It is not common in traditional Korean cooking, but it is often used in salads and juices.

examples.en: I lived in a rented room during college.
I walked around all day to find a room to rent.

examples.ko: 셋방 주인이 다음 달에 월세를 올린대요.
examples.en: The landlord of my rented room says he'll raise the rent next month.
It's a small rented room, but it gets good sunlight.

examples.ko: 좁은 셋방에 가족 네 명이 살았어요.
examples.en: A family of four lived in a cramped rented room.

examples.ko: 셋방살이가 힘들어서 내 집을 갖고 싶어요.
examples.en: Living in a rented room is hard, so I want a home of my own.

explain: 남의 집에서 돈을 내고 빌려 쓰는 방이에요. 요즘은 '월세방', '원룸'이라고 더 많이 말하고, '셋방'은 조금 예스러운 느낌이 있어요. 그런 방에서 사는 것을 '셋방살이'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a room in someone else's house that you pay to use. Today people more often say '월세방' or '원룸', and '셋방' sounds a bit old-fashioned. Living in such a room is called '셋방살이'.

examples.en: In badminton you hit the shuttlecock with a racket.
The wind is blowing, so the shuttlecock keeps flying off.
I bought a new tube of shuttlecocks.
Shuttlecocks are made of feathers or plastic.
I almost got hit by the shuttlecock.
Lots of people play shuttlecock in the park.

explain: 배드민턴에서 치고 주고받는 것으로, 보통 공이 아니라 '셔틀콕'이라고 불러요. '셔틀콕을 치다', '셔틀콕이 넘어가다'처럼 말해요. 가볍고 바람에 약해서 실내에서 하는 경기가 많아요.
explain_en: This is the object hit back and forth in badminton, and people usually call it '셔틀콕' rather than a ball. Typical phrases are '셔틀콕을 치다' and '셔틀콕이 넘어가다'. It is light and affected by wind, so many games are played indoors.

examples.en: After finding a place, I paid a brokerage fee to the realtor.

examples.ko: 소개비가 너무 비싸서 깎아 달라고 했어요.
examples.en: The brokerage fee was too expensive, so I asked for a discount.
You pay the brokerage fee after the contract is done.
I signed the contract directly, without a brokerage fee.
I asked how much I had to pay as a brokerage fee.

examples.ko: 소개비 때문에 이사 비용이 많이 들었어요.
examples.en: Moving cost a lot because of the brokerage fee.

explain: 사람이나 집, 일자리를 이어 준 대가로 내는 돈이에요. 부동산에서는 보통 '중개수수료'라고 하고, 일상에서는 '복비'라고도 말해요. '소개비를 내다/받다/떼다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: This is money paid for connecting people, houses or jobs. For real estate the usual term is '중개수수료', and in daily speech people also say '복비'. Common patterns are '소개비를 내다/받다/떼다'.

examples.en: Two friends are whispering in the back.

examples.ko: 수업 중에 소곤거리면 선생님이 다 들으세요.
examples.en: If you whisper during class, the teacher hears everything.
The child whispered into my ear.
In the library you should talk in whispers.
What are you two whispering about?
I heard whispering and looked back.

explain: 남이 못 듣게 작은 소리로 계속 말하는 모습이에요. '소곤대다'라고도 해요. 남을 흉보듯 몰래 말하는 느낌이 강하면 '수군거리다'를 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It describes talking continuously in a small voice so others can't hear. You can also say '소곤대다'. When the feeling is more of secretly gossiping about someone, '수군거리다' is sometimes used.

examples.en: The kids are chatting in whispers.

examples.ko: 엄마가 소곤소곤 말해서 잘 안 들렸어요.
examples.en: Mom spoke so softly that I couldn't hear well.
I whispered with the person next to me in the theater.
The baby is sleeping, so please speak softly.
I listened closely to the whispering sound.

examples.ko: 둘이 소곤소곤 비밀 얘기를 하고 있어요.
examples.en: The two of them are whispering secrets.

explain: 작은 소리로 조용히 말하는 모양을 나타내서 '말하다', '이야기하다'와 자주 함께 써요. 시끄러운 '떠들썩'이나 '왁자지껄'과 반대되는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It shows a quiet, low-voiced way of talking and often goes with '말하다' or '이야기하다'. It is the opposite in feel of noisy words like '떠들썩' or '왁자지껄'.

examples.en: I can feel the saltiness in the sea breeze.
My face feels sticky because of the salt.

examples.ko: 바다에서 놀고 나서 소금기를 씻어 냈어요.
examples.en: After playing in the sea, I washed off the salt.
This soup has almost no saltiness.

examples.ko: 소금기 있는 땅에서는 농사가 잘 안 돼요.
examples.en: Farming doesn't go well on salty land.

examples.ko: 땀이 마르면 옷에 하얗게 소금기가 남아요.
examples.en: When sweat dries, white salt marks remain on the clothes.

explain: 소금이 들어 있거나 묻어 있는 느낌이나 흔적을 말해요. 음식이 얼마나 짠지는 보통 '간'으로 말해서 '간이 세다/싱겁다'라고 해요. '소금기가 없다/남다/있다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It refers to the feel or traces of salt that is contained in or left on something. How salty food is usually said with '간', as in '간이 세다/싱겁다'. Typical patterns are '소금기가 없다/남다/있다'.

examples.ko: 소기업은 직원 수가 적어서 분위기가 가족 같아요.
examples.en: A small business has few employees, so the atmosphere feels like a family.
The government announced a policy to help small businesses.
It's a small business, but its technology is well recognized.

examples.ko: 소기업에서 일하면 다양한 일을 배울 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you work at a small company, you can learn many kinds of work.
The heads of small businesses gathered and held a meeting.
When the economy gets worse, small businesses suffer first.

explain: 뉴스에서는 '중소기업'이라는 말을 훨씬 많이 쓰고, '소기업'은 그중에서도 규모가 작은 회사를 가리켜요. 반대로 큰 회사는 '대기업'이라고 해요.
explain_en: In the news '중소기업' is used far more often, and '소기업' points to the smaller ones among them. The opposite, a large company, is '대기업'.

examples.en: The children play house with dolls.
When I was little, I played house with my friend.
I bought a play-house toy set as a gift.
My daughter took the mom role in the house-playing game.

examples.ko: 소꿉놀이는 주로 집안일을 흉내 내는 놀이예요.
examples.en: Playing house is mostly a game of imitating housework.
The alley where we used to play house is still the same.

explain: 아이들이 밥 짓기나 가족 역할을 흉내 내며 노는 놀이예요. '소꿉장난'과 거의 같은 뜻으로 쓰고, '소꿉놀이를 하다'와 '소꿉놀이하다' 모두 괜찮아요.
explain_en: This is a children's game of imitating cooking and family roles. It means almost the same as '소꿉장난', and both '소꿉놀이를 하다' and '소꿉놀이하다' are fine.

examples.en: When I was little, I often played house.

examples.ko: 소꿉장난하듯 가게를 차렸다가 금방 문을 닫았어요.
examples.en: They opened a shop as if playing house and soon closed it.

examples.ko: 소꿉장난 같은 연애는 이제 그만하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to stop dating that's like a childish game.
The child sets a table with toy play dishes.
This isn't child's play, it's a real job.

examples.ko: 소꿉장난 속 아빠 역할은 늘 제가 했어요.
examples.en: In our house-playing game, I always played the dad.

explain: 아이들이 소꿉으로 집안일을 흉내 내며 노는 것이에요. 어릴 때부터 함께 놀던 친구는 '소꿉친구'라고 해요. 어른의 일이 어설프고 진지하지 않을 때 비유로도 써요.

phrases.example: 회사 일을 소꿉장난처럼 하면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: You shouldn't treat work at a company like child's play.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일을 진지하지 않고 어설프게 할 때 비판하듯 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used critically when someone does something in a non-serious, amateurish way.

explain_en: It is the children's game of imitating housework with toy kitchenware. A friend you have known since playing together as a child is a '소꿉친구'. It is also used figuratively when an adult's work is clumsy and not serious.

examples.en: Please don't spread this story to anyone.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 내 비밀을 온 동네에 소문냈어요.
examples.en: That person spread my secret all over the neighborhood.
Please spread the word to your friends that the shop is open.
It's a good restaurant, so I want to tell everyone about it.
It would be a problem if you spread this around.
I didn't mean to spread it around on purpose.

explain: 소문을 일부러 퍼뜨릴 때 써요. 나쁜 소문뿐 아니라 좋은 가게나 기쁜 소식을 널리 알릴 때도 쓸 수 있어요. 스스로 퍼지는 것은 '소문나다'(소문이 나다)를 써요.
explain_en: It is used when someone deliberately spreads a rumor. It can be about bad gossip, but also about a good shop or happy news. When it spreads by itself, use '소문나다' (소문이 나다).

examples.en: The firefighters put out the fire quickly.
To become a firefighter, you need to be physically strong.
I met the firefighter and said thank you.

examples.ko: 불난 건물에 갇힌 사람을 구하려고 소방대원들이 투입됐어요.
examples.en: Firefighters were sent in to rescue people trapped in the burning building.

examples.ko: 소방대원은 화재뿐 아니라 구조 일도 해요.
examples.en: Firefighters handle rescue work as well as fires.
My uncle works as a firefighter.

explain: 불을 끄고 사람을 구하는 일을 하는 팀의 한 사람이라는 느낌이에요. 보통 사람을 가리켜 말할 때는 '소방관'이라는 말을 더 자주 들어요. 불을 끄는 일뿐 아니라 구조와 응급 출동도 해요.
explain_en: The feel is of a member of a team that puts out fires and rescues people. When referring to the person, '소방관' is heard more often. Their work includes rescue and emergency calls as well as firefighting.

examples.en: In Japan you pay consumption tax when you buy things.
Opinions were divided over the consumption tax increase.
When the consumption tax rate rises, people tighten their wallets.
Consumption tax is included in this price.
Prices went up because of the consumption tax.

examples.ko: 일본 여행 때 외국인은 소비세 환급을 받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: When traveling in Japan, foreigners can get a consumption tax refund.

explain: 물건이나 서비스를 살 때 가격에 붙는 세금을 말해요. 한국에서 가격에 붙는 세금은 보통 '부가가치세'(부가세)라고 하고, '소비세'는 일본 등 다른 나라 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It means the tax added to the price when you buy goods or services. In Korea the tax added to prices is usually called '부가가치세' (부가세), while '소비세' often appears in news about Japan and other countries.

examples.en: I put the greens in a basket.
I scooped the boiled noodles out with a basket strainer.
I bought a bamboo basket at the market.
Grandma gave me a basketful of potatoes.
A basket like this has holes, so the water drains out.
I need one more basket.

explain: 대나무나 싸리로 엮어 둥글고 넓게 만든 그릇으로, 물기를 빼거나 채소를 담을 때 써요. 뭐든 담는 '바구니'보다 부엌이나 시장 느낌이 강해요.
explain_en: It is a wide, round container woven from bamboo or similar material, used to drain water or hold vegetables. Compared with the all-purpose '바구니', it has a stronger kitchen or market feel.

examples.ko: 소화전 앞에는 차를 세우면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not park in front of a fire hydrant.
There is a fire hydrant in the building's hallway.

examples.ko: 불이 나면 소화전 문을 열고 호스를 꺼내요.
examples.en: If a fire starts, you open the hydrant door and take out the hose.
I learned how to use a fire hydrant in safety training.
Parking is prohibited near the roadside hydrant.
Water was leaking from the hydrant, so I reported it.

explain: 불을 끌 물을 쓸 수 있게 만든 설비예요. 손으로 들고 쓰는 '소화기'와 달리, 소화전은 물과 호스가 연결돼 있어요. 길에도 있고 건물 안 복도에도 있어요.
explain_en: It is equipment that provides water for fighting fires. Unlike a hand-held '소화기' (fire extinguisher), a '소화전' is connected to water and a hose. You find them on streets and in building hallways.
